name: Didong
note: A Gayo performance tradition combining poetry, song and movement.

name: Baju Seting
note: This bridal blouse is made from velvet or silk and paired with cual cloth.

name: Busana pengantin Melayu Bengkulu
note: Women’s bridal clothing includes velvet baju kurung decorated with golden ornaments.

name: Pangsi Banten
note: This loose shirt-and-trouser outfit is associated with Banten’s jawara tradition.

name: Makuta
note: Makuta is ceremonial wedding attire worn by men in Gorontalo.

name: Lacak
note: The lacak is a head covering worn with Jambi Malay men’s ceremonial dress.

name: Pangsi Sunda
note: A practical Sundanese outfit with a loose shirt and trousers, commonly in black.

name: Ludruk
note: East Javanese folk theatre combines everyday stories with humor, music and dance.

name: Batik dan blangkon gaya Surakarta
note: The Surakarta blangkon is a regional form of the folded Javanese headcloth.

name: Chai kue
note: These Chinese-Indonesian dumplings in West Kalimantan can contain jicama, taro or chives.

name: Gence ruan
note: Grilled snakehead fish is topped with a spicy sauce made from chillies and seasonings.

name: Gonggong
note: These edible sea snails are commonly boiled and served with a spicy dipping sauce.

name: Ketupat Kandangan
note: Rice cakes from Kandangan are served with snakehead fish and a seasoned coconut-milk sauce.

name: Kalumpe
note: Pounded cassava leaves are cooked with seasonings in this Dayak vegetable dish.

name: Kepiting soka
note: Tarakan is known for soft-shell crab harvested shortly after moulting, while its shell is still tender.

name: Seruit
note: Fish is shared with shrimp-paste sambal, fermented durian and fresh vegetables.

name: Busana nona rok
note: This formal ensemble pairs a white kebaya with a pleated skirt and a silver waist clasp.

name: Baju Koja
note: Green and yellow distinguish this clothing tradition for young members of the nobility.

name: Rimpu Bima
note: In Bima, rimpu uses two sarongs to cover the head and upper body and wrap the lower body.

name: Daging asap se’i
note: This East Nusa Tenggara specialty slowly smokes meat, commonly beef or pork, over wood.

name: Pakaian kulit kayu khombow
note: At Asei on Lake Sentani, painted khombow bark was traditionally used for clothing.

name: Kain tari sre-a
note: Arfak women’s Tumbu Tanah dress now uses a long cloth wrapped from chest downward.

name: Hiasan hidung kerang Asmat: bipanew
note: Historical Asmat bipanew ornaments were made from shell and worn by men through the pierced nasal septum.

name: Songket Siak
note: This woven textile comes from Siak and was once associated with its royal court.

name: Busana adat Minahasa
note: Minahasa women wear embroidered kebaya with a long cloth at ceremonial occasions.

name: Suntiang
note: Minangkabau brides wear this elaborate tiered headdress.

name: Babu Nggawi
note: A Tolaki ceremonial outfit worn by women.

name: Kain adat Toraja
note: Woven cloth is part of Toraja ceremonial attire.

name: Sarung sutra Mandar
note: Lipaq Saqbe is a woven silk sarong worn with Mandar ceremonial clothing.

name: Pembuatan perahu sandeq
note: Mandar boatbuilders craft slender sailing outriggers called sandeq.

name: Tari Tenun Songket
note: This dance portrays the daily work of women weaving South Sumatran songket.

name: Seruling Lalove
note: This traditional Kaili wind instrument is associated with healing rituals.

name: Lompat batu fahombo
note: In Nias, performers leap over a tall stone structure in the fahombo tradition.
